paragraphs: Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhinai. (Of the first generation of the amoraim of the Land of Israel.)

Shabbat 49a relates: Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhinai and Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar were sitting, with Rabbi Ḥanina bar Ḥama sitting beside them, and a question arose. Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar said to him … Rabbi Ḥanina bar Ḥama said to him, “Thus said Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosi” … They were again sitting, and a question arose. Rabbi Ḥanina bar Ḥama said to him … Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar said to him, “Thus said Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yosi ben Lakunya.”[^1]

notes.text: The ellipses represent Hyman’s abbreviated account: he does not supply the questions or the intervening answers. The translation preserves the named speakers and does not decide the unspecified recipients of “to him.” ר״ח is Rabbi Ḥanina, spelled out earlier in the same passage; ר״ש is rendered by the conventional name Rabbi Shimon. The heading follows the supplied spelling עכינאי rather than silently replacing it with the earlier provisional עכנאי. The generational classification is Hyman’s statement. Shabbat מט. is conventionally rendered 49a, without a claim to have checked a named edition. No new native-page or boundary review was performed.
